mainTopic: How death and שחיטה affect a hanging limb (ניפול), how רבי יוחנן's view fits רבי מאיר, and why רבי יוחנן's rule was needed despite the משנה
overview: First the גמרא checks רבי מאיר's earlier statement about a fetus's limb and a hanging limb. Under רבי שמעון בן לקיש it fits, because רבי מאיר was speaking according to the חכמים's view. Under רבי יוחנן it is a קשיא. So the גמרא restates the dispute: for רבי יוחנן, everyone agrees that שחיטה does not make an animal's own hanging limb count as 'fallen off' (ניפול). רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains why: the hanging limb is part of the mother's body, but the fetus's limb is not. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that everyone agrees מיתה makes a hanging limb ניפול and שחיטה does not. The גמרא asks why he needed to say this, since a משנה seems to teach both rules already. It answers that the משנה's plural word 'הוכשרו' could mean two kinds of flesh, so the משנה alone does not prove the rule for the limb. Finally רב יוסף supports רב יצחק בר יוסף's report, because רבה בר בר חנה agrees. He brings a ברייתא about hanging limbs and flesh, and רבה בר בר חנה's comment on it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Under ריש לקיש, רבי מאיר's statement fits
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי שמעון בן לקיש, רבי מאיר's earlier statement can be explained: he was arguing using the חכמים's own view, while he himself treats both kinds of limbs the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי שמעון בן לקיש, it works: רבי מאיר was speaking to the חכמים using their own view. He meant, 'For me, there is no difference between a fetus's limb and an animal's hanging limb. They are the same.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי מאיר's earlier statement makes sense if we follow רבי שמעון בן לקיש's version of the dispute. The 'בשלמא' wording also sets up a contrast that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן לקיש holds that רבי מאיר argues about hanging limbs just as he argues about fetuses' limbs. So when רבי מאיר seemed to treat the hanging limb differently, he was only using the חכמים's view to make a point. In his own opinion, the two limbs have the same law.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it works out well for... (usually followed by 'but for the other view it is difficult')
He was speaking according to their view, not his own
There is no difference
A limb of a fetus
A limb hanging from the animal itself

steps.confusionAlert: 'לדבריהם' does not mean רבי מאיר agrees with the חכמים. He is borrowing their view to make an argument, and his own opinion is that both limbs are the same.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
he was speaking to them according to their words:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי מאיר, and 'them' are the חכמים he was arguing with.

phrases.english: According to me, there is no difference with a limb of a fetus
and there is no difference with a limb of an animal;
they are the same as each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי מאיר's statement by checking it against רבי שמעון בן לקיש's version of the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the speaker's words as spoken according to the other side's view (לדבריהם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's statement seems to contradict his own view that both limbs are the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר was arguing according to the חכמים's view, so there is no contradiction under רבי שמעון בן לקיש.

steps.title: Under רבי יוחנן, the statement is difficult
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי יוחנן's version of the dispute, רבי מאיר's statement cannot be explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יוחנן, it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that the explanation from step 1 does not work under רבי יוחנן's version of the dispute, so רבי מאיר's statement is a problem for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, רבי יוחנן held that everyone agrees about a hanging limb. That means רבי מאיר could not be 'speaking according to the חכמים's view' on that point. So רבי מאיר's statement does not fit either side's position.

keyTerms.meaning: But according to... (the other opinion)
It is difficult; a problem with no answer yet

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan, it is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא... אלא' structure: the explanation that worked for רבי שמעון בן לקיש fails for רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's earlier version of the dispute about hanging limbs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everyone agrees about a hanging limb, רבי מאיר could not be borrowing the חכמים's view. His statement then contradicts the shared position.

steps.title: Restating the dispute in a corrected version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retells the dispute. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says the dispute about hanging limbs matches the dispute about fetuses. רבי יוחנן says that for a hanging limb, everyone agrees slaughter does not make it count as 'fallen off.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, it was said like this. רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: just as there is a dispute about fetuses, so there is a dispute about limbs. רבי יוחנן said: the dispute is only about a fetus's limb. But about an animal's own hanging limb, everyone agrees that slaughter does not make it count as 'fallen off.'
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of forcing an answer, the גמרא answers the קשיא by saying the dispute between רבי שמעון בן לקיש and רבי יוחנן was really said in a different form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What changed is רבי יוחנן's position on the hanging limb. Now everyone, including רבי מאיר, agrees that slaughtering the animal does not turn its hanging limb into a limb that fell off. That fits רבי מאיר's statement, which treated the hanging limb differently from the fetus's limb.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, it was said like this (introducing a corrected version of a dispute)
Dispute
Everyone agrees
Ritual slaughter
'Fallen off', treated like a limb that fell off the animal before the slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: Only רבי יוחנן's view really changes here. רבי שמעון בן לקיש's position is basically the same as before.
steps.whyThisMatters: This corrected version becomes the main version of the dispute. The rest of the discussion builds on it.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Just as there is a dispute regarding fetuses,
so there is a dispute regarding limbs,
phrases.notes: 'Limbs' here means limbs hanging from the animal itself.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is about the limb of a fetus,
but regarding a limb of an animal,
everyone agrees
slaughter does not make it 'fallen off.'
phrases.notes: He means the slaughter does not make the hanging limb count as if it had already dropped off before the slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by restating the dispute so that רבי יוחנן's view fits רבי מאיר's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the version of the dispute (אי אתמר הכי אתמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's earlier version could not explain רבי מאיר's statement.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוחנן, everyone agrees that slaughter does not make a hanging limb 'fallen off'. רבי מאיר argues only about a fetus's limb.

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר treats the two limbs differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains רבי יוחנן's reading of רבי מאיר: the hanging limb is part of the animal's own body, but the fetus's limb is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: What is the reason for רבי יוחנן's view of רבי מאיר? This one (the hanging limb) is its body, and that one (the fetus's limb) is not its body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asks why, according to רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר treats a hanging limb differently from a fetus's limb, and then gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter is done on the mother animal, so it works on everything that is part of her body. A hanging limb is still part of her body, so the slaughter covers it. The fetus is a separate creature, so its limb is not part of her body and the slaughter does not help it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
According to (the view of)
Its (the animal's) own body

steps.whatToRemember: In the corrected version of רבי יוחנן's view, רבי מאיר says slaughter covers a hanging limb but not a fetus's limb, because only the hanging limb is part of the mother's body.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan
according to Rabbi Meir?
This is its body,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the limb hanging from the animal, and 'that' in the next line is the fetus's limb.

phrases.english: and that is not its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's corrected position from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the slaughter of the mother covers what is part of her body, like a hanging limb, but not a fetus's limb, which is not part of her body.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: death makes 'fallen off,' slaughter does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that everyone agrees מיתה makes a limb count as fallen off (ניפול), and שחיטה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that when an animal dies, its hanging limb counts as if it already fell off. But when the animal is slaughtered, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of רבי יוחנן that sets a rule everyone agrees on: death makes a limb count as 'fallen off,' and שחיטה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a limb counts as 'fallen off,' it is treated as a limb taken from a living animal (אבר מן החי), not as part of a נבלה. רבי יוחנן says death has this effect but שחיטה does not, and that nobody argues about this.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Death of the animal without proper שחיטה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone agrees that death makes 'falling off,'
phrases.notes: He means that once the animal dies, its hanging limb is treated as if it fell off while the animal was still alive.

phrases.english: and slaughter does not make 'falling off.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another statement of רבי יוחנן about how death and שחיטה affect a hanging limb, continuing the discussion of his view of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees: מיתה makes a hanging limb count as fallen off, and שחיטה does not.

steps.title: Which limb is meant, and why say it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which limb רבי יוחנן means. A fetus's limb is openly argued about, and an animal's own limb is already covered by a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If you say a fetus's limb, they do argue about that! Rather, it must be the animal's own limb. But we already learned about death in a משנה, and we already learned about שחיטה too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement. Either it is wrong to say 'everyone agrees,' or it is not needed because a משנה already says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither choice works. For a fetus's limb, the words 'everyone agrees' are false, since רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue. For the animal's own limb, the rule seems pointless, because a משנה already teaches both death and שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say
Fetus

steps.confusionAlert: 'Death we learned, slaughter we learned' is not agreeing with רבי יוחנן. It is a complaint that his statement adds nothing new.

phrases.english: What are we dealing with?
If you say with a limb of a fetus,
they really do disagree!
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about the fetus's limb, so 'everyone agrees' cannot fit there.

phrases.english: Rather, with a limb of the animal itself,
death we already learned, slaughter we already learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement in step 5 by asking which case it covers.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that everyone agrees about מיתה and שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it means a fetus's limb, 'everyone agrees' is false. If it means the animal's own limb, it is already taught in a משנה and adds nothing.

steps.title: The משנה that already teaches the rule for death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: when the animal dies, its hanging limb is impure as אבר מן החי and not as נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned about death: if the animal died, the hanging flesh needs הכשר. The limb makes things impure as a limb from a living animal, not as a limb from a נבלה. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the rule for death is already taught, to back up its complaint from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the hanging limb as אבר מן החי once the animal dies, meaning death made it count as 'fallen off.' No one is recorded as disagreeing, so this is the same 'everyone agrees' rule that רבי יוחנן stated.

keyTerms.meaning: Making food able to become impure, through contact with a liquid
A limb taken from a living animal, which makes things impure
An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: Death we already learned:
If the animal died, the flesh needs to be made susceptible to impurity,
phrases.notes: This is the hanging flesh. It is treated like ordinary food, which only becomes impure after touching a liquid.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאֵבֶר מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי,
phrases.english: and the limb makes things impure as a limb from a living animal,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אֵבֶר מִן הַנְּבֵלָה;
phrases.english: and does not make things impure as a limb from a carcass;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim 'death we already learned' in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule 'death makes ניפול' is already taught
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה: when the animal dies, the limb is impure as אבר מן החי, not as נבלה (רבי מאיר, with no one recorded as disagreeing).

steps.title: The משנה that already teaches the rule for slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about שחיטה: רבי מאיר says the animal's blood makes the hanging parts susceptible to impurity, and רבי שמעון says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned about שחיטה: if the animal was slaughtered, the hanging parts were made susceptible to impurity by its blood. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון says: they were not made susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the rule for שחיטה is already taught, finishing its proof that רבי יוחנן's statement seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון treat the hanging parts as food that needs הכשר. They only argue about whether the blood does the job. So both agree the limb is not אבר מן החי after שחיטה, meaning שחיטה does not make 'falling off.' This is exactly רבי יוחנן's second half.

keyTerms.meaning: They were made susceptible to impurity by its blood
Also
Blood, one of the liquids that can make food susceptible to impurity

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has shown that both halves of רבי יוחנן's rule, for death and for שחיטה, already seem to appear in a משנה. So it now has to explain why רבי יוחנן needed to say it.

phrases.english: Slaughter, too, we already learned:
If the animal was slaughtered, they were made susceptible by its blood,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the hanging limb and the hanging flesh.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Shimon says: they were not made susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for 'slaughter we already learned,' the second half of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule 'שחיטה does not make ניפול' is already taught
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same משנה: after שחיטה, רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue only about הכשר through the blood, so both treat the limb as food and not as אבר מן החי.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן still needed to say it
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone, one could think 'הוכשרו' refers only to the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that משנה, I would have thought: what does 'they were made susceptible' refer to? Only the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6: why did רבי יוחנן need to state a rule the משנה seems to teach already?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the משנה alone, one could say 'הוכשרו' is only about the hanging flesh. Then the hanging limb might be treated as fallen off at שחיטה, with its own impurity of אבר מן החי. רבי יוחנן's rule closes that door: שחיטה does not make the limb count as fallen off.

keyTerms.meaning: They were made able to receive impurity
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
On the flesh: referring only to the flesh

phrases.english: If we learned it only from that one,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the משנה about שחיטה quoted in Step 8.

phrases.english: I would have said:
What is 'they were made susceptible'? It refers to the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'we already learned it' half of Step 6's challenge (שחיטה תנינא). It shows that the משנה quoted in Step 8 could be read as speaking only of the flesh, so רבי יוחנן's rule was still needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the earlier source was open to a different reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הוכשרו' means only the flesh, so שחיטה could make the limb count as fallen off.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's statement is needed to rule out this reading.

steps.title: But the משנה uses the plural
steps.stepSummary: The plural 'הוכשרו' seems to include both the limb and the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'they were made susceptible', in the plural!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 9's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the flesh were meant, the משנה should use the singular. The plural seems to point to both the limb and the flesh, and then the משנה would already teach רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches: pointing to the exact wording of a source

phrases.english: But it teaches 'they were made susceptible'!
phrases.notes: The word is plural, so it sounds like more than one thing, the limb and the flesh.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'הוכשרו' refers only to the flesh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural form suggests two items, the limb and the flesh.

steps.title: Two kinds of flesh
steps.stepSummary: The plural covers flesh coming off the animal and flesh coming off the limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say: one is for flesh separating from the animal, and one is for flesh separating from the limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the plural can still mean only flesh, just two kinds of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of hanging flesh: flesh hanging from the animal's body, and flesh hanging from the hanging limb. 'הוכשרו' in the plural could cover these two, so the limb itself is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: You might say: offering a possible reading
Flesh coming off the hanging limb

phrases.english: You might say:
one is for flesh that separates from the animal,
and one is for flesh that separates from the limb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the plural challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plural can mean two kinds of flesh, so the משנה alone does not prove רבי יוחנן's rule.

steps.title: Why mention both kinds of flesh?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes one kind of flesh different enough to need its own mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what makes this one stronger than that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to cover both kinds of flesh. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both kinds of flesh follow the same rule, saying it once should be enough. So the גמרא wants to know what we might have gotten wrong about one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Its strength: what makes it a stronger case

phrases.english: And what is the strength of this one over that one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the two-kinds reading of Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why both kinds of flesh need to be taught.

steps.title: Flesh from the limb still needs הכשר
steps.stepSummary: Since flesh on the limb shares the limb's strong impurity, we might think it needs no הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: since it gives the strong impurity together with its 'father' (the limb), it should not need הכשר. So the משנה teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why flesh coming off the limb had to be mentioned separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flesh attached to an אבר מן החי is impure with the limb's strong impurity. So we might think that flesh has its own impurity and needs no הכשר. The plural teaches that once it is apart, it still needs הכשר like regular flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind: a mistaken first thought
Severe impurity, here the impurity of אבר מן החי
Because of its 'father': as part of the limb it is attached to
It teaches us: this is the new point

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say,
since it gives off severe impurity
because of its father,
phrases.notes: 'Its father' is the limb the flesh was attached to.

phrases.english: I would say it does not need to be made susceptible,
so it teaches us that it does.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Flesh from the limb might have been thought to need no הכשר because of the limb's severe impurity; the משנה teaches it does need הכשר.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'הוכשרו' could mean two kinds of flesh, so it does not prove the limb is not treated as fallen off. That is why רבי יוחנן's rule was needed.

steps.title: רב יוסף: hold on to רב יצחק בר יוסף's report
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says to accept רב יצחק בר יוסף's report of רבי יוחנן, because רבה בר בר חנה agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Hold on to what רב יצחק בר יוסף said, because רבה בר בר חנה stands with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף backs up the version of רבי יוחנן's rule that שחיטה does not make a hanging limb count as fallen off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף tells us to accept רב יצחק בר יוסף's report of רבי יוחנן: שחיטה does not make a hanging limb count as fallen off. His support is that רבה בר בר חנה, also quoting רבי יוחנן, holds the same view. The next step shows where.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold in your hand: accept this as correct
Stands with him: holds the same view

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: נְקוֹט דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף בִּידָךְ,
phrases.english: Take the statement of Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef in your hand,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה קָאֵי כְּוָותֵיהּ.
phrases.english: because Rabba bar bar Chana holds like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: נְקוֹט דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining why the rule was needed to supporting it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יצחק בר יוסף's version of רבי יוחנן (שחיטה does not make it ניפול) is right.

steps.title: The ברייתא about hanging limbs and flesh
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that hanging limbs and flesh stay forbidden even after שחיטה. Then רבה בר בר חנה's comment is introduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'Flesh torn in the field you shall not eat' comes to include a limb or flesh hanging on an animal, wild animal or bird; even if one slaughtered them, they are forbidden. And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב יוסף's claim. It is setting up רבה בר בר חנה's statement, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules that a hanging limb or flesh stays forbidden even after שחיטה. רבה בר בר חנה's explanation of this ברייתא in the name of רבי יוחנן will show he agrees that שחיטה does not make the limb count as fallen off.

keyTerms.meaning: Torn: here, meat forbidden to eat
Hanging: partly cut off but still attached
To include: the פסוק adds this case

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
'And flesh torn in the field you shall not eat'
this comes to include the limb and the flesh
that are hanging on a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird,
and he slaughtered them, that they are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רב יוסף's claim in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That רבה בר בר חנה agrees with רב יצחק בר יוסף's report of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שמות 22:30, plus רבה בר בר חנה's comment in the name of רבי יוחנן (which follows).
